sup-754d8ad360ab94d0-w12:c.i.hint: Separate the reflected part of the incoming sunlight from the part that is absorbed.
notes: Albedo is reflected solar power divided by incident solar power. For an opaque surface, absorbed fraction is 1 − albedo.
Use the same system boundary for numerator and denominator. For a planet, add reflected contributions that leave the planet; do not count outgoing infrared as reflected sunlight.

sup-754d8ad360ab94d0-w12:c.ii.hint: Draw an energy boundary around the whole planet. Which incoming and outgoing arrows cross that boundary?
notes: A spherical planet intercepts sunlight over πR² but emits over 4πR². In the simplest equilibrium model, (1 − α)S/4 = εσT⁴.
At equilibrium, absorbed solar power equals outgoing thermal power. Surface and atmospheric transfers are internal to the whole-planet budget, so do not count them twice.

sup-754d8ad360ab94d0-w16:a.i.hint: Identify which objects gain energy and which lose it. Does the temperature change, or is there a change of state?
notes: Use Q = mcΔT within one phase, and Q = mL for a phase change. Break a multi-stage heating process into separate energy terms.
For an insulated mixture, energy lost equals energy gained. Include the container’s heat capacity if it is supplied; a temperature difference has the same value in K and °C.

sup-754d8ad360ab94d0-w16:b.i.hint: Identify what stays fixed: amount of gas, temperature, pressure or volume. Use only the simplification that those conditions allow.
notes: Use pV = nRT = NkT with absolute pressure and kelvin temperature. For a fixed amount, p₁V₁/T₁ = p₂V₂/T₂.
If gas leaks or moves between containers, the amount in one container may change. Apply conservation of total molecules to the complete closed system instead of assuming pV/T is fixed locally.

sup-754d8ad360ab94d0-w16:b.ii.hint: Treat the gas as the system and mark the directions of heat and work before substituting numbers.
notes: With W positive for work done by the gas and Q positive into it, ΔU = Q − W. “Rejects heat” makes Q negative; compression makes W negative.
For an ideal gas, internal energy depends on temperature. An unchanged temperature does not by itself mean no heat or work transfer.
For “show that”, start from the supplied data and display the intermediate steps. Do not substitute the result you are asked to show as an assumption.

sup-754d8ad360ab94d0-w16:b.iii.hint: Draw the energy entering from the hot reservoir, the useful work and the energy rejected to the cold reservoir.
notes: Over a complete engine cycle ΔU = 0, so W = Q_hot − Q_cold and efficiency = W/Q_hot. Use energy per cycle or power consistently.
Only an ideal reversible Carnot engine reaches η = 1 − T_cold/T_hot. Both reservoir temperatures must be in kelvin; this gives an upper bound for a real engine.

sup-754d8ad360ab94d0-w16:c.hint: Consider the system and its surroundings together. A local entropy decrease need not violate the second law.
notes: For reversible heat transfer at constant temperature, ΔS = Q_rev/T. A warming or cooling reservoir uses the sign of the heat it receives.
The total entropy of an isolated system cannot decrease. Irreversible processes increase total entropy and reduce the energy available for useful work; energy itself is still conserved.
